description: The locational banking statistics of the Bank for International Settlements measure international banking activity from a residence perspective, by the location of the banking office, consistent with balance of payments principles. They record the outstanding claims and liabilities of internationally active banks located in reporting countries against counterparties in more than 200 countries, on an unconsolidated basis that includes intragroup positions, and capture about 95 per cent of all cross-border banking activity. A currency breakdown and reported breaks in series let the BIS compute break- and exchange-rate-adjusted changes that approximate quarterly flows. The data are quarterly, in US dollars, not seasonally adjusted, and overseen by the Committee on the Global Financial System, with methodology, reporting countries, reporting practices and breaks documented. Access is free on the BIS data portal with bulk downloads and an API under the BIS terms of permitted use (unrestricted with citation). Caveats: positions are aggregates by country pair, not by bank, and some countries' data are carried forward. For simulation it gives the cross-border banking network between countries for financial contagion and exposure analyses. Related catalogue records include the BIS CPMI Red Book statistics and GLEIF LEI data.
